Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Kiwi players get in the huddle before they take their positions out in the middle. Mohammad Naim and Soumya Sarkar will open the innings for Bangladesh. Tim Southee to bowl first up. Here we go...

Finn Allen has been caught for a little chat before the action begins. He says that it was good to bat out there. Tells that he was a bit nervous with all the talks of this being his home ground. Adds that Guptill kept him calm and terms batting with him as awesome. Mentions that they took a couple of balls to get into it and then decided that it was time to go big. Adds they need to bowl well to win the game.

Right! The target for Bangladesh is 142. It is a big score in front of them but the good thing is that they know what they have to achieve to register their first win of the tour. Will they be able to do so? We will find out in a short while.

You got to feel for the bowlers. On a ground where the boundaries are short, they had to bowl with a wet ball. Once again the fielding from Bangladesh was poor as they failed to grab the chances that came their way and eventually paid the price. Mahedi after getting smashed for 16 runs off his first 3 balls of the spell, got the wicket of Guptill. However, if they thought things will ease down a bit, they were wrong. Allen kept smashing them all over the park. Shoriful delivered a decent penultimate over where he gave just 9 runs and got the wicket of Phillips. Taskin did well in the final over as he gave 10 and got a wicket too. Overall, a tough outing for the Bangladeshi bowlers.

Guptill and Allen came in and went bang, bang. It was Allen who became the aggressor as he played the reverse sweep. He played the conventional sweep. He hit down the ground and he smashed through the covers. Guptill too was looking really well as the Kiwis reached 50 in the 4th over of the match. Guptill fell in the 6th over but not before smashing 44 off just 19 balls. However, it was Allen who did all the damage on his way to a fiery half ton. Phillips couldn't do much as he departed for 14 off 6 balls. Allen eventually got out for 71 off just 29 balls in the final over of the innings.

19 runs and 3 wickets in the final 2 overs and Bangladesh will be slightly pleased with their effort in the last 2 overs. However, they were once again poor in the field and failed to grab their chances and have eventually been smashed for 141 in the 10 overs. A terrific knock from Allen as far the Kiwis are concerned.

OUT! RUN OUT! There was never two there! A suicidal run but it was probably the last ball so they had to go for it. It is full and outside off, Mitchell jams it out towards mid off. They take one. Chapman wants another. The fielder throws it to the keeper who whips the bails off. Mitchell is well short. So a decent last over by Taskin. NEW ZEALAND END WITH 141!
Mark Chapman is in now.
Two! Shorter and on middle, Mitchell pulls it through mid-wicket for two.

OUT! TAKEN! Fin Allen's enterprising innings comes to an end! He looks to innovate, tries to play the paddle scoop but this is a good slower one from Taskin on middle. It goes off the top edge towards short third man. Hasan there runs back and takes a good tumbling catch.
Just the one but once again Mitchell could have put that away! It is a slower one on a length. DM swings but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It rolls on the off side for one.

Mitchell misses out! This is a full toss, it is mistimed wide of long on. Naim does well, runs to his right, slides, picks the ball up and parries it to the man running towards him from deep mid-wicket. Two taken.
FOUR! A boundary to begin the last over then! It is full and right where Mitchell likes it. He hits it down the ground. Good start to the last over.
A dot to end! End of a good spell by Shoriful! The last ball is a yorker on middle, Allen hits it hard back towards the bowler who sticks a hand out and stops it.
Taskin Ahmed to bowl the last over of the innings.
Bowls a yorker but does so well wide outside off. Mitchell fails to jam it out. Wided.

The bowler gets nowhere near it in the end! Allen once again steps out and Islam bangs it short. Allen looks to flat-bat it but hits it high up in the air towards mid-wicket. Islam calls for it. He does not look comfortable under it and in the end, does not even lay a hand on it. Two taken.
FOUR! In the gap and a boundary! Allen comes down the track, Islam bowls a slower short ball. Allen is done in by the pace but still manages to drag it wide of long on for a boundary.
Mitchell is off the mark! It is shorter and on the body, DM nudges it on the leg side for one.
Daryl Mitchell is in now. 10 balls left in the innings. You know what he will think of doing.

OUT! Bangladesh finally hang onto one! This is really nicely bowled. Full and outside off, not easy to get under those. Glenn fails to get the elevation he wanted and hence, hits it straight to mid off. Sarkar there makes no mistake.
Shorter and outside off, this is slapped down to long on for one.
Who will bowl the penultimate over of the innings? Shoriful Islam it will be. Gave 12 in his first. What can he do? New Zealand will be eying 150.
A single to end! So 13 from this over as well. On the pads, it is worked through square leg for one.
SIX! Another present for Allen and he accepts it gleefully. A full toss on the pads, it is whipped over the square leg fence for a biggie.

FOUR! That has been misjudged! This is a full toss outside off. Allen once again fails to time it. Since he had to reach for it, he does not get the power. It goes high up in the air towards deep cover. The fielder runs to his right and also runs in a little. It falls behind him and goes for a boundary.
Well bowled again! Glenn shows his intentions to the bowler early, he lines up to play the switch hit. Hasan bowls it wide outside leg. Phillips hits it down to long off for one.
Well bowled! A yorker, just inside the tramline outside off. Phillips looks to carve it but misses.
Allen comes down the track and whips it through mid-wicket for one.

SIX! BANG! Down the ground this time. Massive over again. A slower one from Rubel but it is wide outside off and fuller in length. Phillips uses the long handle and pumps it down the ground for a biggie.
SIX! Phillips goes big now! What a strike from him. A good length ball, right in the hitting arc. And Phillps says thank you very much and powers it over deep mid-wicket. 100 up for the Kiwis.
Fullish and around middle, it is paddled down to deep square leg for a run.
Length ball around off, slapped to sweeper cover for one.

In the air... put down. It was another tough chance but maybe these needs to be taken at this level. A short ball, just outside off. Allen goes after it but ends up getting a top edge. The ball goes high in the air. The fielder from long off comes running in from his position. He dives forward and gets a fingertips to it but fails to hold on.

FOUR! That is hit like a tracer bullet. What a shot to get to the maiden half ton in T20Is. It has taken just 18 balls for Allen to get there. A length ball, it is the slower one. Allen clears his front leg and hammers it past the bowler and into the fence at long off.
A single to end an action-packed over! Outside off, it is hit through covers for one.
FOUR! Nice and fine now! Not a good delivery after picking a wicket on the last ball. This is full and on the pads, this is worked fine and it goes to the fine leg fence.
Glenn Phillips has been promoted up the order.

OUT! TAKEN! Good change in field and Bangladesh have broken through the opening stand which was batting them out of the game! The cover had been pushed back and Hasan bowls another low full toss outside off. Guptill continues to go after it but this time he does not time it that well. He had to reach out for it and hence, it is not off the middle. He holes out to the fielder in the deep. Can Bangladesh manage to pull things back a little?
FOUR! Make that 16 now! This is not a bad delivery but Guptill is in his zone. A low full toss outside off. Guptill gets under it and lofts it over covers for a boundary.

SIX! Two in a row for Guptill! He is into the 40s now. This is played more on line. It is on the pads and Guptill sweeps it over the square leg fence for another biggie. 12 from the first two balls. This is going to be another expensive over.
SIX! That is right off the bottom but it still goes over the fence! It is fired outside off. Guptill flat-bats it down the ground. Not off the middle but away from the fielder and over the fence.
Bowling change! Mahedi Hasan is on now.
Swing and a miss! Another slower one, well disguised. Allen is early in the heave and he misses. A rare dot and Bangladesh need a lot more of these.
On middle, this is pushed down to long on for one. This was nicely bowled, closer to the batter, not letting him free his arms.
Two more! Shorter and outside off, Guptill looks to slap it over covers but it goes off the toe-end over the fielder there for two.
Just a single! A slower one, it is mistimed to long on for one.
SIX! Smack! Allen is in his element! He expects it short and makes room. Gets it and he slaps it well over the point fence. 10 from Rubel's first two balls.

FOUR! Welcome into the attack, Rubel! That is why you can't drop quality players! The paddle scoop is out. It is on middle and Allen hits it over the short fine leg fielder. It goes for a one-bounce boundary.
Rubel Hossain to bowl the 5th over of the innings.

Put down! Another tough chance but this one was easier than the last one. Still though, in this night sky, this is not easy. It is on a length, another slower one. Allen swings but early. He splices it high up in the air towards point. Hossain spills it. One more taken. These missed chances can cost Bangladesh big time.
FOUR! Just wide of cover! Allen dealing in boundaries! This is a length ball outside off, it is slapped wide of the fielder at sweeper cover. Boundary.
FOUR! Smashed! That is a gift but it still has to be put away. 50 up for the Kiwis. It is on middle, Allen smashes it back past the bowler for another boundary.
Dropped! Not an easy chance that! It is a slower one. Allen looks to go over mid off but mistimes it. Rubel, the fielder there runs back and then dives forward but fails to take it. Two taken.
A loud appeal but turned down! Allen comes down the wicket and this is banged in short. Allen looks to pull but misses.
A slower one on off, it is pushed towards cover for one.
Shoriful Islam is into the attack now.

A single to end but a huge over for the Kiwis! Nasum bowls it very full and on middle, Guptill looks to sweep but gets an inside edge towards short fine leg for one. End of the Powerplay and the Kiwis are off to a flier.
It has started to drizzle.
This is fired on middle, Allen pushes it down to long on for one.

SIX! Over the fence! 18 from the first 4 balls. Allen is on fire. Showing all the shots he can play. Now makes use of the feet, gets to the pitch of it and smashes it over the bowler's head for a biggie.
FOUR! Make that three in a row! Really good batting from Allen! He is playing it with the angle as he knows there is no spin. Shuffles across and hits it in the gap in the mid-wicket region.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries! Through the leg side this time. Allen plays it with the angle. He whips it through mid-wicket for another boundary.

FOUR! That is not a good effort in the field! Islam is the man, he should have stopped that. Allen plays the reverse sweep. He does not time it that well and gets it over point. Islam hares after it. The ball is slowing up as it gets to the ropes. Islam dives forward and tries to push it back in but fails to do so.
Mistimed but two! 14 from the over then! Taskin bowls another well-disguised slower one. It is well outside off. Guptill goes after it. It flies off the toe-end over point for two.
Good from the pacer! Goes short and on the body, Guptill looks to pull but misses.
SIX! Guptill is dealing in biggies! His third. This is right in his arc, full and on middle, Guptill lofts it downtown and it goes all the way.
Good comeback! A slower one on middle, Guptill pushes it to covers.
SIX! He has picked the bones out of that one! Wow! That is a colossal hit! It is shorter and angled into the body. Guptill smashes it high and over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Back of a length, angling into the body of the batter, cramping him for room. It is guided to point.
Taskin Ahmed to bowl from the other end.
Dot to end the over! Flat and just outside off, Allen punches it hard but finds the cover fielder. 9 off the opening over.
Shortish and around middle, it is forced wide of mid on for a quick single. 9 off the 5 balls of the first over.
Flat and just outside off, cut to the point fielder.
SIX! BANG! This time he bangs it hard and long. A short ball, Guptill rocks back and slams it via pull over deep mid-wicket for a biggie.

Two and Guptull and New Zealand are underway. Floated just around off, Guptill just lifts it over mid off. Fails to time it as well as he would've liked but it is good enough to clear the man in the ring and fetch two for him.
Guptill almost dragged on there! A flat ball just around off, Guptill makes room and looks to cut. Manages to chop it just past the stumps and behind keeper.

And finally, it is time for the action. The Bangladeshi players stride out in the middle, following the two umpires. Martil Guptill and Fin Allen make their way out as well. Nasum Ahmed to bowl first up. All set now. Here we go...

Pitch report - Craig McMillan is down for the pitch report. He says that the pitch is a big greasy due to the rain. Adds that the outfield is a bit soggy as well. Praises the groundsmen for doing a great job after all the rain around. Adds it is quite amazing that we are getting a game here.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Mohammad Naim, Liton Das (C/WK), Soumya Sarkar, , Najmul Hossain Shanto (IN FOR MAHMUDULLAH), Afif Hossain, Mahedi Hasan, Mosaddek Hossain (IN FOR MOHAMMAD SAIFUDDIN), Nasum Ahmed, Shoriful Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Rubel Hossain (IN FOR MOHAMMAD MITHUN).

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Martin Guptill, Finn Allen, Devon Conway (WK), Will Young, Glenn Phillips, Mark Chapman, Daryl Mitchell, Tim Southee (C), Tod Astle (IN FOR ISH SODHI), Adam Milne, Lockie Ferguson (IN FOR HAMISH BENNETT).

Tim Southee, the Kiwi skipper, says it has been a great season and he hopes they can finish well. States they have had enough time to switch on and it should be an exciting game. Informs Astle comes in and Ferguson comes in and it is quite exciting to have Milne and Ferguson together in the side. Ends by saying he has enjoyed captaincy and leading the young side.

Liton Das says they want to bowl first because of the weather. States the conditions are similar to the last game where bowling was tough. Ends by saying they are looking to win this game and they want end well.
TOSS - The two captains are out in the middle. It is Liton Das for Bangladesh and Tim Southee for New Zealand. Tim tosses it up and it lands in Bangladesh's favor. They will BOWL FIRST.
We have a start time as well. After the toss, the action will begin at 2110 local. The news is that is is going to be a 10-over game with a 3-over Powerplay.
Update 2040 local - More good news! The players are out warming up... we probably aren't far away from action. TOSS AT 2055 LOCAL, as said, we aren't far away from the action to begin.
Update 1957 local (0657 GMT) - Good news! The rain has stopped and the covers seem to be coming off. The conditions overhead also look better and the umpires are out there, having a look.
Update 1950 local (0650 GMT) - Nothing new to share as the drizzle continues and keeps us away from any action. Stay tuned.
Update 1920 local (0620 GMT) - Nothing much to update as it continues to drizzle at Eden Park. All we can do is hope things get better and we get some action.

Taskin Ahmed is in for a little chat as well. He tells that in T20Is in New Zealand, due to the shorter boundaries, even the good balls go for boundaries and you got to feel for the bowlers. Adds that still needs to keep things simple and stick to basics. Says they tried their best. Tells they have played with wet ball in night games at home. Terms the conditions in the last game difficult for the bowlers. Feels they did a lot of mistakes in the previous game in the fielding and it becomes costly. On his catch of Guptill in the last game, Taskin says that he watched the ball till the last moment and tried to catch.

Finn Allen was caught for a little chat a while back. He starts by saying that it was nice to get off the mark in the 2nd game. Adds it was a bit frustrating in the first game. Tells that it was nice to cross the line in the previous game. On him playing an amazing shot to get off the mark, Finn says that he has been doing that successfully so he just tried and it worked. Adds he doesn't want to change anything but believes it is going to be a bit tougher in international cricket. Says he just tries to keep things simple and believes in watching the ball and hitting it. Mentions that he has never played in Auckland and the short boundaries on this ground are exciting.

Update 1850 local (0550 GMT) - The rain stopped. And the covers were taken off. But maybe only for just 5-odd minutes as drizzle returned. And the covers are back on again. It is going to be that kind of a day.
Update 1835 local (0535 GMT) - As expected, the toss has been delayed with the covers on. However, a few Kiwi players are on the ground and having a chat.

Weather update - Well, the conditions right now isn't promising. The covers are firmly in place with a light drizzle on. Also, there was an New Zealand Women and Australia Women locked horn on this very venue in the afternoon and that game didn't last even 3 overs due to the persistent rain. So, fingers crossed.

We have a news and it is not a good one if you are a Bangladesh fan. Mahmudullah has been ruled out of this game due to an injury which he sustained during the second T20I. In his absence, Liton Das will be leading the side.

However, the Kiwis will have a clean sweep on their mind. Looking at their form, that is pretty much possible. Their batting is firing. The quick bowlers are giving hard times to the Bangladeshi batters aided by Sodhi's brilliance with spin. They will look to put on a collective performance one last time to end their home session on a high. Rain can act as a villain in this game. So, stay with us as we bring you the toss, weather and team updates.

Three ODIs done! Two T20Is done! One remains. And it is time for that last T20I game and the last chance for Bangladesh to head home with at least one victory under their belt. It has been a tough, tough tour for them. They had their chances in both ODIs as well as T20Is but they failed to grab the opportunity. The Bangla Tigers will hope to trump the Kiwis in this game though.
